Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Somalia's National Communications Authority price index (2026) shows cheapest data bundles around $0.40-0.50/GB, and Cable.co.uk (2025, via Digital Banking News) puts Somalia at $0.19/1GB — both well under 1% of the ~$620 (2024) GNI per capita per month, corroborating the StatRanker/ITU-derived 0.8% figure. Score 5 confirmed with three independent sources.

Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Comments: AU PIDA project entry indicates Somalia IXP project under 'Construction (2022)', implying planned/under development rather than established broad participation.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The African IXP Association (Af-IX) lists the Somali Internet Exchange Point (SoIXP, Mogadishu) as an established/active IXP since 2018, operated by SomaliREN — contradicting the AU PIDA entry's 'under construction (2022)' status. AFRINIC/whois records confirm registered peering (AS37781) and management (AS328363) ASNs, but participation appears limited to SomaliREN-affiliated networks with no major ISPs listed as peers on PeeringDB/IXPDB. Revised to 3 (single IXP with limited participation).

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
Comments: DataReportal citing GSMA Intelligence reports 11.3M mobile connections in early 2025, equivalent to 58.3% of population; used as proxy for mobile penetration (connections, not unique subscribers).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original score used a connections-based proxy (58%), but the variable specifically requires unique subscriber penetration. GSMA's own Mobile Economy MENA 2023 report states Somalia's mobile penetration rate is 'below 40%', and ITU data (via TheGlobalEconomy.com) shows only 53.96 subscriptions per 100 people in 2023 — itself inflated relative to unique subscribers by multi-SIM ownership. Recalculated to 2 (25-39%) as the best estimate; exact unique-subscriber percentage was not published, so flagged for human review to confirm precise banding.

Definition: Percentage of mobile connections using smartphones (as opposed to feature phones or basic phones). Smartphones are the minimum device requirement for accessing most digital public infrastructure services, apps, and mobile internet.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, though the underlying figure is a proxy rather than a direct measure. DataReportal's newer Digital 2026: Somalia report (Nov 2025, citing GSMA Intelligence) shows 75.7% of mobile connections are now 3G/4G/5G ('broadband'), still within the 60-79% band. No Somalia-specific smartphone-adoption percentage was found in GSMA's Africa smartphone report; broadband-technology share remains an imperfect substitute since some broadband connections are used with non-smartphone devices.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Regional cloud availability zone nearby (same sub-region)
Comments: No hyperscale cloud region in Somalia found; nearest major hyperscale regions include AWS Middle East (Bahrain/UAE) and Azure Qatar as described in regional cloud expansion reporting, implying regional zones nearby but not local.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: No hyperscale cloud region operates within the Horn of Africa or East Africa; the nearest AWS/Azure regions remain Middle East (Bahrain/UAE) and South Africa (af-south-1, Cape Town) — arguably outside Somalia's own sub-region rather than 'nearby, same sub-region'. A Tier III colocation facility (Wingu Africa, Berbera) exists but is not a hyperscale cloud zone. Value kept at 3 pending human review of whether Middle East/South Africa should count as 'same sub-region' under this variable's scale, or whether code 2 (distant regions only) is more accurate.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
Comments: Somalia enacted Data Protection Act (effective March 2023) and established/launched Somalia Data Protection Authority (officially launched Feb 2024), indicating enacted law with authority.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed directly on the Somalia Data Protection Authority's own website (dpa.gov.so), which cites Data Protection Act No. 005 of 2023 (in force 23 March 2023) and confirms the Authority's independent regulatory role; Digital Policy Alert confirms the DPA was formally inaugurated on 24 February 2024. Score 4 (legislation enacted with DPA established) confirmed with primary sources.

Definition: The presence and tier quality of commercial/colocation data center facilities operating in the country. Commercial data centers provide the physical infrastructure for hosting cloud services, content delivery, and enterprise applications domestically.
Comments: DataCenterMap lists 1 data center facility in Somalia (market: Berbera). This suggests small-scale/commercial presence rather than multiple Tier III+ facilities.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: DataCenterMap/Baxtel list only one internationally tracked facility, but it is explicitly a Tier III carrier-and-cloud-neutral facility (Wingu Africa, Berbera, commissioned 2021, part of a pan-East African network), not Tier I-II as the original comment inferred. Locally operated providers (e.g. Dalkom Somalia, Eurosom in Mogadishu) also advertise data centre services, though these are not independently tier-verified. Revised to 3 (at least one Tier III facility) on the strength of the Wingu Berbera facility.

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
Comments: Somali Household Budget Survey (as summarized by U.S. International Trade Administration) reports urban electricity access 80.1% vs rural 39.4% in 2023; gap = 40.7 percentage points (falls in 21–40pp band; borderline just over 40).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The World Bank's own indicators (rural: 23.9% in 2023, EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS) and Somalia's National Bureau of Statistics SDG7 report (urban rising to 79%, rural falling to 23.9%, 2023) give a gap of 55.1 percentage points — larger than the trade.gov-derived 40.7pp figure and falling in the 41-60pp band rather than 21-40pp. Recalculated to 2 on the strength of official World Bank/national statistics data.

Comments: UN e-government knowledgebase city data page shows Somalia EGDI 2024 = 0.29710, which falls in 0.25–0.49 band.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original source cited was the UN's City-level data page for Mogadishu (a Local Online Service Index figure), not the national EGDI. The UN e-Government Knowledgebase's own Compare Countries tool gives Somalia's actual national EGDI 2024 as 0.1468 (rank 191, group L2 — Low), well below the 0.25 threshold used for the Middle band. Recalculated to 1 (EGDI <0.25, Low); this is a material downward correction based on the correct primary indicator.
